sentences.zh: 嗨，我是里奇。

sentences.en: Me too.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: I want a talk show with me as the hoSt.
sentences.zh: 我想要一个由我主持的脱口秀。

sentences.en: You want to talk about current events?
sentences.zh: 你想谈论时事吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: What kind of stuff do you want to talk about?
sentences.zh: 那你想谈论什么样的话题？

sentences.en: Me.
sentences.zh: 我。

sentences.en: How much will that cost?
sentences.zh: 那要花多少钱？

sentences.en: $15 million.
Oh, and I want to come in on a swan boat.
sentences.zh: 哦，我还想坐着天鹅船出场。

sentences.en: You're off your meds, you're living in a reservation casino, and you're hosting your own talk show.
sentences.zh: 你没吃药，住在预留的赌场里，还要主持自己的脱口秀。

sentences.en: It's a new era.
sentences.zh: 这是一个新时代。

sentences.en: $86 million, Alice.
sentences.zh: 8600万美元，爱丽丝。

sentences.en: We go live in 5, 4, 3.
sentences.zh: 我们5、4、3准备直播。

sentences.en: I think she's a little frozen.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她有点僵住了。

sentences.en: You're on TV now.
sentences.zh: 你现在上电视了。

sentences.en: I'm Alice Klieg, and welcome to me.
sentences.zh: 我是爱丽丝·克里格，欢迎来到我的世界。

sentences.en: So Richard, why is this?
sentences.zh: 那么理查德，这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why is it that when we receive money from certain sources, the way we think about spending that money changes dramatically?
sentences.zh: 为什么当我们从特定来源获得金钱时，我们考虑花钱的方式会发生巨大的变化？

sentences.en: You know, one of my colleagues, my fellow troublemakers, is David Leibson, who's just become the chairman of the Harvard Economics Department.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的同事之一，也是我的捣蛋同伙，大卫·莱布森，他刚刚成为哈佛经济系的主任。

sentences.en: Used to be one of my protégés.
sentences.zh: 他曾经是我的门生之一。

sentences.en: Now, you know.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道的。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: Some of my friends had a roast for me a couple weeks ago because I had a big birthday.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我的一些朋友为我举办了一场吐槽大会，因为我过了一个大生日。

sentences.en: And he was telling the following story.
sentences.zh: 他当时讲了下面这个故事。

sentences.en: A bunch of us were invited to Washington, must have been 15 years ago, when David was a struggling young assistant professor,
sentences.zh: 我们一群人被邀请去华盛顿，那一定是在15年前，当时大卫还是个苦苦挣扎的年轻助理教授，

sentences.en: and did something for the National Institute of Health.
sentences.zh: 为美国国立卫生研究院做了一些工作。

sentences.en: And they gave us a $200 honorarium for the day.
sentences.zh: 他们给了我们200美元作为当天的酬金。

sentences.en: So I was saying, you know, this is ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时说，你知道，这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: We don't work for $200 a day.
sentences.zh: 我们不会为了每天200美元而工作。

sentences.en: We have to go out and spend this money on dinner.
sentences.zh: 我们得出去把这笔钱花在晚餐上。

sentences.en: And so we went out and had a good dinner.
sentences.zh: 于是我们出去吃了一顿美餐。

sentences.en: You could get quite a good dinner for $200 15 years ago.
sentences.zh: 15年前，200美元确实能吃到一顿相当不错的晚餐。

sentences.en: Now, David was not happy about spending $200 on dinner.
sentences.zh: 现在，大卫对花200美元吃晚餐并不高兴。

sentences.en: And he now claims it was more like $300 when I got done with the wine.
sentences.zh: 他现在声称，等我喝完酒，账单更接近300美元。

sentences.en: But, you know, this was my way of thinking, I'm not going to work for $200.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这是我的思维方式，我不会为了200美元而工作。

sentences.en: But I'm happy to have a good dinner as a result of helping out the NIH.
sentences.zh: 但我很高兴能因为帮助了国立卫生研究院而享用一顿美餐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So studies have found also, for example, that if you want to reward employees at the end of the year, giving them a cash bonus is very different than giving them a vacation.
sentences.zh: 研究还发现，例如，如果你想在年底奖励员工，给他们现金奖金与给他们度假机会是非常不同的。

sentences.en: That even though you're giving them the same amount of money, you're giving them, let's say, $500 as a bonus versus $500 as a vacation.
sentences.zh: 尽管你给他们的钱数相同，比如给他们500美元奖金，或者500美元的度假费用。

sentences.en: People report being significantly happier when you give them the vacation than when you give them the cash.
sentences.zh: 人们报告说，当你给他们度假机会时，他们比给他们现金时要快乐得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, because if you give them the vacation, they get to go guilt-free.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为如果你给他们度假机会，他们可以毫无负罪感地去享受。

sentences.en: I rediscovered this last week with my daughter.
sentences.zh: 上周我和女儿在一起时重新发现了这一点。

sentences.en: And I made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 我犯了一个错误。

sentences.en: And it's a mistake people shouldn't have made.
sentences.zh: 这是一个人们本不该犯的错误。

sentences.en: But I had good reasons.
sentences.zh: 但我有充分的理由。

sentences.en: And I was well-intentioned.
sentences.zh: 而且我是出于好意。

sentences.en: So my daughter's a Mets fan.
sentences.zh: 我女儿是大都会队的球迷。

sentences.en: And one of the Mets pitchers happens to be a neighbor.
sentences.zh: 而大都会队的一名投手恰好是我们的邻居。

sentences.en: So she was an avid Mets fan.
sentences.zh: 所以她是一个狂热的大都会队球迷。

sentences.en: And I thought it would be nice to buy her two tickets to one of the first-round games when her neighbor was pitching.
sentences.zh: 我觉得如果能给她买两张第一轮比赛的票，正好是她邻居投球的那场，会很不错。

sentences.en: But I got this idea late.
sentences.zh: 但我这个想法产生得太晚了。

sentences.en: So I went online.
sentences.zh: 所以我上网查了。

sentences.en: And I found that I could get tickets for about $400.
sentences.zh: 我发现票价大约要400美元。

sentences.en: And, but I didn't have time to buy the tickets and mail them to her.
sentences.zh: 但是，我没有时间买票并邮寄给她。

sentences.en: So I sent her an email with a link to this website saying, look, it looks like you can get tickets for $400 each.
sentences.zh: 所以我给她发了一封邮件，附上了这个网站的链接，说，看，看起来你可以以每张400美元的价格买到票。

sentences.en: I'm going to send you $1,000, buy two tickets on this website.
sentences.zh: 我要给你寄1000美元，在这个网站上买两张票。

sentences.en: And she had already expressed great excitement about getting to go to this game.
sentences.zh: 她之前已经表达了对能去看这场比赛的极大兴奋。

sentences.en: So I sent her that email.
sentences.zh: 所以我给她发了那封邮件。

sentences.en: I get back a text.
sentences.zh: 我收到了一条短信。

sentences.en: LOL, this is just like one of the examples from your book.
sentences.zh: 哈哈，这就像你书里的例子之一。

sentences.en: If you send me $1,000, I'm not going to spend it on baseball tickets.
sentences.zh: 如果你给我寄1000美元，我才不会把它花在棒球票上。

sentences.en: So now she would have been happy to, if I had sent her the tickets, for sure they would have gone to the game.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我直接寄给她票，她肯定会很高兴去现场看比赛。

sentences.en: But I send her the $1,000, nothing.
sentences.zh: 但我寄给她1000美元，结果什么都没发生。

sentences.en: So I didn't send her the $1,000.
sentences.zh: 所以我没给她寄那1000美元。

sentences.en: More of my conversation with behavioral economist Richard Thaler after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后继续我和行为经济学家理查德·塞勒的对话。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Back in the 1970s, Stanford psychologist Walter Mischel conducted a series of experiments that came to be known as the marshmallow teSt.
sentences.zh: 早在20世纪70年代，斯坦福大学心理学家沃尔特·米歇尔进行了一系列实验，后来被称为“棉花糖测试”。

sentences.en: Small children were put in a room and told they could either get one marshmallow right away.
sentences.zh: 小孩子们被带进一个房间，被告知他们可以马上得到一颗棉花糖。

sentences.en: But if they stayed in the room and didn't eat the marshmallow, they would get a second.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们留在房间里不吃掉那颗棉花糖，他们就能得到第二颗。

sentences.en: Children who tried not to eat the first marshmallow came up with ways to distract themselves.
sentences.zh: 那些试图不吃掉第一颗棉花糖的孩子想出了各种分散注意力的方法。

sentences.en: Watching these children on video is hilarious.
sentences.zh: 看着这些孩子在视频里的表现真是太搞笑了。

sentences.en: All right, here's the deal.
sentences.zh: 好了，交易是这样的。

sentences.en: Marshmallow for you.
sentences.zh: 这是给你的棉花糖。

sentences.en: You can either wait, and I'll give you another one if you wait, or you can eat it now.
sentences.zh: 你可以等一等，如果你等的话，我会再给你一颗，或者你现在就把它吃了。

sentences.en: When I come back, I'll give you another one.
sentences.zh: 等我回来，我会再给你一颗。

sentences.en: So then you'll have two.
sentences.zh: 这样你就有两颗了。

sentences.en: But stay in here and stay in the chair until I come back, okay?
sentences.zh: 但要待在这里，坐在椅子上直到我回来，好吗？

sentences.en: I played Richard Thaler a video of a marshmallow test in progress where a small boy tries desperately not to eat the marshmallow placed in front of him.
sentences.zh: 我给理查德·塞勒播放了一段正在进行的棉花糖测试视频，视频中一个小男孩拼命忍住不吃面前的棉花糖。

sentences.en: At one point, he leans lovingly into the marshmallow and takes a great big sniff, and then sadly looks away.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他深情地凑近棉花糖，用力闻了一下，然后悲伤地转过头去。

sentences.en: How'd you do?
sentences.zh: 你表现得怎么样？

sentences.en: Did you do good?
sentences.zh: 你做得好吗？

sentences.en: You did?
sentences.zh: 你做到了？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You wanted to eat it, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 你很想吃掉它，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So did I tell you I'd give you another one?
sentences.zh: 那我有没有告诉你我会再给你一颗？

sentences.en: The excited boy cramps both marshmallows, chipmunk style, into his mouth.
sentences.zh: 那个兴奋的小男孩像花栗鼠一样把两颗棉花糖都塞进了嘴里。

sentences.en: So talk about self-control, Richard.
sentences.zh: 那么谈谈自控力吧，理查德。

sentences.en: Why have classical economics ignored the idea that humans have trouble with self-control?
sentences.zh: 为什么古典经济学忽略了人类在自控力方面存在困难这一观点？

sentences.en: So economic theory says that we optimize and that we always choose what's best for us.
sentences.zh: 经济理论认为我们追求最优，并且总是选择对我们最有利的结果。

sentences.en: So that includes self-control.
sentences.zh: 所以这包括了自控力。

sentences.en: And so, you know, in these experiments, if you would rather have two marshmallows than one, you should be willing to wait ten minutes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在这些实验中，如果你宁愿要两颗棉花糖而不是一颗，你就应该愿意等待十分钟。

sentences.en: But as, you know, obviously kids have less self-control than adults, so this experiment kind of exaggerates that.
sentences.zh: 但显然，孩子们比成年人的自控力差，所以这个实验有点夸大了这一点。

sentences.en: But what you get from those videos, those precious videos, is the real important idea, which is that self-control is work.
sentences.zh: 但从那些珍贵的视频中，你得到的是一个真正重要的观点，那就是自控力是一种工作。

sentences.en: Resisting temptation is work.
sentences.zh: 抵制诱惑是一种工作。

sentences.en: This is important.
sentences.zh: 这一点很重要。

sentences.en: You know, 30% of Americans are obese.
sentences.zh: 你知道，30%的美国人肥胖。

sentences.en: Half of Americans are not saving enough for retirement.
sentences.zh: 一半的美国人没有为退休存够钱。

sentences.en: So these are enormous problems that we as a society face, and they are at their core because exerting self-control is difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是我们作为一个社会面临的巨大问题，它们的核心原因就是行使自控力非常困难。

sentences.en: In some of these marshmallow experiments, they used Oreos.
sentences.zh: 在一些棉花糖实验中，他们使用了奥利奥饼干。

sentences.en: And my favorite one of these, in one condition, there was a kid, and he had three Oreos in front of him.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一个案例是，在某种情况下，有个孩子面前有三块奥利奥。

sentences.en: And he could have one now, but he was looking at the three.
sentences.zh: 他现在可以吃一块，但他一直盯着那三块看。

sentences.en: And what he does is, as soon as the person leaves the room, he opens up the Oreos, licks out the middle, and then puts them back together.
sentences.zh: 他做的是，当那个人一离开房间，他就打开奥利奥，舔掉中间的夹心，然后把它们重新合上。

sentences.en: And I have a deep suspicion, these were done many years ago at Stanford.
sentences.zh: 我有一个强烈的怀疑，这些实验是多年前在斯坦福大学做的。

sentences.en: I'm pretty sure that guy is Bernie Madoff.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定那个人就是伯尼·麦道夫。

sentences.en: There's interesting work that you've cited by George Lowenstein and others looking at the difference between hot and cold emotional states,
sentences.zh: 你引用过乔治·洛温斯坦等人的有趣研究，探讨了热和冷情绪状态之间的区别，

sentences.en: which is that if you ask me right now, would you be able to resist having dessert at lunch, I would say, yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，如果你现在问我，午餐时你能抵制住吃甜点的诱惑吗，我会说，是的，当然。

sentences.en: I can probably resist having dessert at lunch.
sentences.zh: 我可能能抵制住午餐时吃甜点的诱惑。

sentences.en: But an hour and a half from now, when I'm really hungry and I'm sitting down at the table and there's dessert in front of me,
sentences.zh: 但一个半小时后，当我真的很饿，坐在桌边，面前摆着甜点时，

sentences.en: the person whom I am at that point is very different than the person I am right now.
sentences.zh: 那一刻的我与现在的我截然不同。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, you know, we can all relate to that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们都能感同身受。

sentences.en: We all know the hazards of going to the grocery store hungry.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道饿着肚子去杂货店的危险。

sentences.en: And let's say you're there on Thursday and you missed lunch and it's 6 o'clock and you're buying dinner not just for tonight but also for Saturday.
sentences.zh: 假设你在周四去那里，错过了午餐，现在是6点钟，你买的晚餐不仅是今晚的，还有周六的。

sentences.en: Now, your hunger now should not affect the size of the roast you buy for Saturday.
sentences.zh: 现在，你当下的饥饿感不应该影响你为周六购买的烤肉大小。

sentences.en: But, you know, you'll buy a bigger roaSt.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你还是会买一块更大的烤肉。

sentences.en: The other thing, of course, we often do sometimes when we have problems with self-control is that we try and have an external enforcer.
sentences.zh: 当然，当我们有自控力问题时，我们经常做的另一件事就是尝试寻找一个外部执行者。

sentences.en: We try and appoint somebody who will help us run that kind of self-control.
sentences.zh: 我们试图指定某人来帮助我们执行那种自控力。

sentences.en: This, of course, goes back to the old idea, the myth of Ulysses who was sailing by the sirens.
sentences.zh: 这当然可以追溯到古老的观点，即尤利西斯航行经过塞壬海妖的神话。

sentences.en: He was afraid that he was going to drift close to the sirens.
sentences.zh: 他担心自己会漂流到靠近塞壬的地方。

sentences.en: And so Ulysses had his men bind him to the mast of his ship so that they would be able to sail close to the sirens and hear the siren song without actually being tempted to go toward the sirens.
sentences.zh: 于是尤利西斯让手下把他绑在船桅上，这样他们就能靠近塞壬，听到塞壬的歌声，而不会真的被诱惑去靠近塞壬。

sentences.en: So people have tried variations of this and all kinds of things to try and address the temptations that we expect to face in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以人们尝试了各种变体和各种方法，试图应对我们预期在未来会面临的诱惑。

sentences.en: I came by a very nice clip from the TV show Curb Your Enthusiasm where Larry David is essentially asked to be the enforcer for one of his friends.
sentences.zh: 我偶然发现了一段来自电视剧《抑制热情》的非常好的片段，拉里·大卫基本上被要求担任他朋友的执行者。

sentences.en: Take a look at the clip.
sentences.zh: 看看这个片段。

sentences.en: So, you hungry?
sentences.zh: 那么，你饿吗？

sentences.en: Starving.
sentences.zh: 饿死了。

sentences.en: Good, we got a great meal and some fabulous desserts, which, by the way, I need you to keep me away from no matter what.
sentences.zh: 很好，我们有很棒的餐点和美味的甜点，顺便说一下，无论如何你都要让我远离它们。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yeah?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Because I put a lot of time into this.
sentences.zh: 因为我在这上面花了很多时间。

sentences.en: I need like a dessert referee.
sentences.zh: 我需要一个甜点裁判。

sentences.en: All right, I'm your guy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我就是你要找的人。

sentences.en: You promise?
sentences.zh: 你保证？

sentences.en: Yeah, I promise.
sentences.zh: 好的，我答应你。

sentences.en: Okay, I'm counting on you.
sentences.zh: 行，那我就指望你了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: No, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: I'm just going to have a bite.
sentences.zh: 我就吃一口。

sentences.en: Oh, no, no, no, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不，不，不，不，不，不。

sentences.en: Just a bite, come on.
sentences.zh: 就吃一口，拜托。

sentences.en: Oh, you know what?
sentences.zh: 噢，你知道吗？

sentences.en: But you told me specifically not to let you have any dessert.
sentences.zh: 但你特意嘱咐过我，绝对不能让你吃甜点。

sentences.en: I appreciate it, Larry, but I changed my mind.
sentences.zh: 我很感激，拉里，但我改变主意了。

sentences.en: Yes, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 是，是，是。

sentences.en: But you said no matter what.
sentences.zh: 但你说了无论如何都不能吃。

sentences.en: But you know what?
sentences.zh: 但你知道吗？

sentences.en: I'm changing it.
sentences.zh: 我现在改主意了。

sentences.en: And this is now I'm saying thank you for helping me.
sentences.zh: 这就是我为什么要谢谢你帮我。

sentences.en: I'm going to have some cake.
sentences.zh: 我要吃点蛋糕。

sentences.en: No, no, but you can't change it.
sentences.zh: 不，不，你不能改主意。

sentences.en: That's why you say no matter what.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你说无论如何都不能吃。

sentences.en: This is the what.
sentences.zh: 现在就是那个“无论如何”的时候。

sentences.en: But now...
sentences.zh: 但现在……

sentences.en: That's why you asked me and not these other people, because you knew I wouldn't let you.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你找我而不是找别人，因为你知道我不会让你吃的。

sentences.en: Larry, give me the cake.
sentences.zh: 拉里，把蛋糕给我。

sentences.en: She told me not to let her have.
sentences.zh: 她告诉过我别让她吃。

sentences.en: I don't care.
sentences.zh: 我不在乎。

sentences.en: She said no matter what, okay?
sentences.zh: 她说无论如何都不能吃，明白吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So that is the hot, cold empathy gap.
sentences.zh: 这就是“冷热共情差距”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So when she was in the cold state, she didn't want any dessert.
sentences.zh: 所以当她处于冷静状态时，她不想吃任何甜点。

sentences.en: When she was staring the dessert in the face, you know, let me at it.
sentences.zh: 当她面对甜点时，你知道的，就想大快朵颐。

sentences.en: So thank you all so much.
sentences.zh: 所以非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: And thanks to Richard Thaler.
sentences.zh: 也要感谢理查德·塞勒。

sentences.en: That was behavioral economist Richard Thaler.
sentences.zh: 刚才那位是行为经济学家理查德·塞勒。

sentences.en: His latest book is called Misbehaving, the Making of Behavioral Economics.
sentences.zh: 他最新的书叫《错误的行为：行为经济学的形成》。

sentences.en: This week's show was produced by Cara McGurk-Allison, Maggie Penman, and Max Nestrack.
sentences.zh: 本周节目由卡拉·麦格克-艾利森、玛吉·彭曼和马克斯·内斯特拉克制作。

sentences.en: Our team includes Tara Boyle, Raina Cohen, Parth Shah, Jennifer Schmidt, and Renee Klar.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队成员包括塔拉·博伊尔、雷娜·科恩、帕斯·沙阿、詹妮弗·施密特和蕾妮·克拉尔。

sentences.en: Our unsung heroes this week are Adam Osman, Nikki Strickland, Thomas Bussey, and Don Gooden.
sentences.zh: 我们本周的幕后英雄是亚当·奥斯曼、尼基·斯特里克兰、托马斯·巴西和唐·古登。

sentences.en: Adam, Nikki, Thomas, and Don work on our facilities team here at NPR,
sentences.zh: 亚当、尼基、托马斯和唐是我们NPR的后勤团队成员，

sentences.en: and they recently helped us move to a new floor of the building.
sentences.zh: 他们最近帮我们搬到了大楼的新楼层。

sentences.en: They intuitively understood how important a good workspace is to being creative and productive.
sentences.zh: 他们凭直觉理解一个好的工作空间对创造力和生产力有多重要。

sentences.en: They put in long hours, including on the weekend,
sentences.zh: 他们投入了很长时间工作，包括周末，

sentences.en: and helped us pack, unpack, and get settled in our new space.
sentences.zh: 帮我们打包、拆包，并在新空间安顿下来。

sentences.en: I'm so grateful for their hard work.
sentences.zh: 我非常感激他们的辛勤工作。

sentences.en: I'm so grateful for their own stuff.
sentences.zh: 我非常感激他们自己的东西。
